# Northwind Telecom — Outages and service levels

*Synthetic document. Northwind Telecom is a fictional operator invented for testing; every figure
below is made up and describes no real product, tariff or person.*

## Knowing about an outage

Planned work is announced to affected connections at least 48 hours ahead, by message and in the
app. Unplanned outages appear in the app's service status panel within 15 minutes of being
detected, with the area affected and an expected restoration time.

## Restoration targets

| Fault | Target |
|---|---|
| Mobile cell outage | restored within 6 hours |
| Fibre node outage | restored within 8 hours |
| Single-premises fibre fault | visit within 24 hours, restored within 48 |
| Cable cut affecting a street | restored within 72 hours |

Targets are measured from the time the fault is detected or reported, whichever is earlier, and
exclude time waiting for access to premises or for a municipal permit to dig.

## Rent credit

A fibre connection down for more than 24 continuous hours earns a credit of one day's rent for each
full day of downtime, applied automatically to the next bill. No claim is needed. Credit is not
given for downtime caused by the customer's own equipment, by a power failure at the premises, or
by a disconnection for non-payment.

## Reporting a fault

Report from the app, which attaches the line's current diagnostics automatically, or by calling
198 from a Northwind connection. A ticket number is issued immediately and every update is sent to
the registered contact.

## Escalation

A ticket that passes its restoration target is escalated automatically to a regional engineer. A
ticket open for more than 72 hours can be escalated by the customer from the app, which routes it
to the nodal officer for the circle.

## During an outage

Mobile connections in an affected area are moved to a neighbouring cell where one is in range, which
usually means a working but slower connection. Fibre connections have no equivalent fallback.
